draft.title: Historical empathy
card: Historical empathy means trying to understand why people in the past acted as they did. We look at their beliefs, their living conditions and the choices they had.
It does not mean judging them only by today's values. Many things people now find wrong were accepted in their time, and people then often did not know what we know.
To use empathy, ask what the person believed, what they knew and what pressures they faced. Then use sources to check your answer.
Empathy is not the same as agreeing with an action or excusing it. A historian can understand why something happened and still say it caused harm.
draft.remember: Explain people's actions by their world, not only by ours.

a.q: Which question shows historical empathy about a medieval villager who believed illness was caused by bad air?
opts: What did people in her village know and believe of illness
Why was she so foolish to ignore modern medicine at the time?
Why did she not think the way people do today?
Was she right to believe what she did about illness?
a.why: Empathy starts by asking what the person knew and believed in her own time. The other questions judge her by modern knowledge and values, which is what empathy avoids.
a.clue: Look for the question about her world, not ours.

b.q: A student says a medieval villager was foolish to fear a comet, as comets are natural. Which reply best shows historical empathy?
opts: Omens were a common belief then, so comets worried people
They should have known better, as comets have natural causes
Their fear shows that people then were less intelligent
Their fear was correct, because comets do bring disasters
b.why: The best reply explains the fear by the beliefs common in the villager's time. The tempting option, that they should have known better, judges them by today's knowledge. Empathy does not mean saying the belief was correct either.
b.clue: Ask what people in that time commonly believed.
